open_obligations: Note that an 8k-step attack budget bounds, but does not exclude, hard-to-find incorrect proofs.
Check whether sneaky-only provers without weight sharing are a stronger attack than Anil et al.'s L-BFGS message optimisation.
Note the domain change from toy tasks to GSM math.
in.other_title: Verifier grows harder to exploit by sneaky-only provers; larger verifiers more robust
in.rationale: Anil et al. note that frozen-verifier stress tests cannot rule out incorrect proofs that are hard to find. Kirchner et al. attack verifiers with separately trained sneaky-only provers and report that steps-to-exploit rise over rounds and that 10^-2-size verifiers were not exploited beyond round 0 within 8k RL steps, while 10^-3 verifiers stayed exploitable until round 4; a stronger attack with a fixed budget still cannot prove no hard-to-find proof exists.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how robust a PVG-trained verifier is to separately trained adversarial provers, for GPT-4-family verifiers on grade-school math

text: The authors evaluate robustness by freezing the verifier and either further training the prover or directly optimizing messages with optimizers such as L-BFGS, which removes the verifier's ability to rely on the prover's 'tell'; they note it remains possible that incorrect proofs exist that the verifier would accept but that are difficult to find.
title: Frozen-verifier stress tests cannot exclude incorrect proofs that are hard to find
